links.outcome: Extraction error rate of LLM versus manual abstraction against adjudicated ground truth
links.effect: LLM error rate 7.0% vs manual abstraction 14.2% (P<0.001) across 8708 datapoints for 28 variables
links.quote: Across 8708 datapoints for 28 variables with only one correct answer, the LLM achieved a 7.0% error rate, outperforming manual abstraction (14.2%, P <0.001).

links.outcome: Error rate reduction with targeted human review of low-confidence AI outputs
links.effect: Targeted human review of 30% of low-confidence AI outputs decreased error rates to 4.4%
links.quote: A hybrid approach with targeted human review of 30% of low-confidence AI outputs further decreased error rates to 4.4%.

links.outcome: Interinstitutional variability in extraction error across 10 centers
links.effect: Interinstitutional variance lower with AI (0.12%) than manual abstraction (0.39%)
links.quote: Interinstitutional variance was lower with AI (0.12% versus 0.39%).

links.outcome: Ground truth defined by concordant sources with blinded expert adjudication
links.effect: Ground truth used concordant values with discrepancies adjudicated by a blinded expert; no comparison of this practice was reported
links.quote: Ground truth was defined as concordant values across sources, with discrepant cases adjudicated by a blinded expert.
